research.summary: The existing deployment domain already verifies immutable releases, compatibility, runtime profiles, optimistic revisions, retained runs, and audit entries, but its public commands accept deployment, run, policy, capability, secret, and egress inputs that normal Publish interaction must not own. The structured repository retains deployment and run records but lacks an atomic current-deployment projection by exact release and host target. The trusted runtime verifies supported exact reference releases but reports Start as an immediate terminal handoff and has no bounded launch descriptor. The current deployment workflow generates identifiers inside a host-owned handler, while its generic presentation still exposes manual identifiers and policy-derived fields. Publish already lists only non-archived systems and correlates each published build to its exact immutable release. The cohesive implementation is therefore an additive lifecycle facade that derives identifiers and policy from trusted composition, reconciles a retained current projection, treats active runs as long-lived sessions, and exposes only bounded state/action projections through parity transports.

risks: Lifecycle reads for multiple published builds can flash stale controls or overwrite a newer workspace selection unless each card owns bounded request state and discards stale responses.
Duplicate action submission can race expected revisions unless every card disables controls through invoke and refresh.
A launch descriptor can be mismatched to a different build unless the surface requires exact release equality before reading the immutable revision.
A runtime may start successfully while visual revision or catalog loading fails; the UI must retain Stop-only state and report launch failure rather than claiming the session stopped.
Closing an automatically opened visual surface must not silently stop or mutate the retained runtime session.
Archived or deleted sources can become stale after initial publication load; lifecycle denial must remove operable controls and refresh must not resurrect them.

Reusing the design renderer must omit design-time claims and expose only registered declarative resources; authored HTML, scripts, URLs, components, Node, filesystem, and host authority remain forbidden.

Removing the Run & Test tab must also remove host-page client construction and static navigation references without deleting the authoritative application workflow family still used by non-routine diagnostics.
Packaged desktop and local browser qualification is exact-environment evidence and does not establish other-platform, physical assistive-technology, or production-capacity claims.
research.summary: Publish already projects active systems and correlates each published build to an exact release and immutable revision. Minimal desktop and thin lifecycle clients exist but are not mounted. Desktop and thin pages still construct the generic Run & Test presenter. The existing bounded System Composition renderer can render only registered side-effect-free Foundation resources from an exact immutable revision, so it can be reused as the automatic visual surface after matching an application-issued launch descriptor to the selected published release. Routine lifecycle UI therefore needs no deployment, run, capability, secret, egress, policy, URL, path, component, or executable input.
